result.title: SPLICE: Sparse Physics Library Identification and Compositional Expansion
result.summary: Neural operator splitting composes a library of neural operators, one per physical mechanism, into zero-shot simulators of new equations. Existing approaches, however, require these mechanisms and their labels to be specified in advance. We ask whether a pretrained library can instead be adapted and grown from unlabeled trajectories in which multiple mechanisms act simultaneously. We introduce SPLICE, a framework that discovers operators without mechanism labels on mixture data. The contributions of the candidate operators to each trajectory are inferred by solving a convex optimization problem. A calibrated test then assigns each discovered operator the mechanism it implements. Failure cases are also detectable, when the library lacks the required physics or when mechanisms are insufficiently separable. Across one and two dimensional systems, the discovered operators recover mechanisms from unlabeled mixtures and compose into zero-shot simulators of unseen equations; a frozen library can also grow an operator for physics absent from pretraining, without labels and without forgetting. On Navier-Stokes, the discovered operators compose about as accurately as their supervised counterparts.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SPLICE，用凸优化从无机制标签的混合轨迹中推断各候选神经算子的贡献，再以校准检验为发现的算子指派其所实现的机制，从而零样本组合模拟新方程，并可在冻结库上无标签、无遗忘地扩展新机制。
AI.relevance_reason: 其无标签推断多个模块对状态的贡献、以及在库缺少所需机制或机制不可分时检测失败，可能为 LVR 的 latent 贡献分配、证据/机制缺失识别与停止决策提供跨领域启发，可供核查。
